CreateCapacityReservation.description:
When the reservation job completes, the HTTP API pushes a message as follows: > The HTTP API is a method for receiving messages about session start, stop, streaming, and other events. Currently, messages are retained for 1 Day, and the retry policy is backoff retry, with a maximum of 176 retries. The event type is `CAPACITY_RESERVATION_RESULT`. >Regardless of pattern, messages are pushed only through the HTTP API.> | Name | Type | Required | Description | | ------ | ------ | ------ |----- | | success | Boolean | Yes | Indicates whether the job succeeded.
Valid values:
true: The job succeeded.
false: The job failed. | | eventType | String | Yes | The event type. | | eventDetail | Object[EventDetail] | Yes | The event details.
This parameter is returned only when the job succeeds. | The data structure of EventDetail is as follows: | Name | Type | Required | Description | | ------ | ------ | ------ |----- | | taskId | String | Yes | The job ID. | | success | Boolean | Yes | Indicates whether the job succeeded.
Valid values:

false: The job failed. | | projectId | String | Yes | The project ID. | | appId | String | Yes | The application ID. | | appVersion | String | Yes | The Application Version. | | districtId | String | Yes | The area ID. | | expectSessionCapacity | Integer | Yes | The expected number of sessions to be supported. | | realSessionCapacity | Integer | Yes | The actual number of sessions supported by the produced containers. |

DescribeInstanceStatsInfo.title: Query instance statistics
DescribeInstanceStatsInfo.summary: This API queries statistics information about Graphic Computing Service instances purchased by users, across various dimensions. You can use this API to obtain instance statistics information based on conditions such as Project ID (ProjectId), District ID (DistrictId), and Instance Type (InstanceType). The instance statistics information includes the number of instances in states such as creating, running, O&M, and releasing.
DescribeInstanceStatsInfo.responseParamsDescription:
### Return example

Normal return example in JSON format.

```
{
    "RequestId": "46329898-489C-4E63-9BA1-C1DA5C5D0977",
    "Data": [
        {
            "ProjectId": "6733705348307226241003",
            "DistrictId": "huabei",
            "InstanceType": "gcs.r1c1m1.1xlarge",
            "TotalCount": 4,
            "RunningInstanceCount": 1,
            "OperatingInstanceCount": 1,
            "ReservingInstanceCount": 1,
            "ReleasingInstanceCount": 1
        }
    ]
}
```

ReleaseCapacity.title: Release Reserved Container
ReleaseCapacity.description:
The operation to release a reserved container is atomic, meaning there is no scenario of partial success or partial failure. When the release job succeeds, the HTTP API sends a notification message as follows: > The HTTP API is a method for receiving notifications about session start, stop, streaming, and other events. Currently, messages are retained for 1 Day, and the retry policy is a backoff strategy with up to 176 retries. The event type is `RELEASE_CAPACITY_RESULT`. >Pattern is not distinguished; notifications are pushed only via the HTTP API.> | Name | Type | Required | Description | | ------ | ------ |----|------ | | success | Boolean | Yes | Indicates whether the job succeeded.
Valid values:
true: The job succeeded.
false: The job failed. | | eventType | String | Yes | The event type. | | eventDetail | Object[EventDetail] | Yes | The event details.
This parameter is returned only when the job succeeds. | The data structure of EventDetail is as follows. | Name | Type | Required | Description | | ------ | ------ |----|------ | | taskId | String | Yes | The ID of the asynchronous container release job. | | success | Boolean | Yes | Indicates whether the release succeeded.
Valid values:
true: The release succeeded.
false: The release failed. | | expectReleaseSessionCapacity | Integer | Yes | The expected number of ingest endpoints of sessions to release. |
